What

What Oak Tree Care Involves

Oak tree care is the species-specific maintenance of red and white oaks — structural and deadwood pruning to ANSI A300 standards, oak wilt assessment, root-zone protection, and dormant-season scheduling built around the disease. Because oaks anchor NE Ohio's mature canopy, the work is as much about preservation as it is about pruning: keeping a heritage tree structurally sound for another generation rather than defaulting to removal.

The distinction that matters with oaks is timing. Oak wilt (Bretziella fagacearum) is vectored by sap-feeding beetles during the April-through-July active season, and every fresh cut is a direct entry point. Roubic never prunes oaks between April 1 and July 31 — all oak work is scheduled for the dormant season (December-March) or late summer (August-October), the only safe windows.

Why

Four Reasons Homeowners Call Roubic for Oaks

The oak scenarios Aaron walks most often across NE Ohio's heritage-canopy neighborhoods.

A Red Oak Wilting From the Top

Rapid upper-canopy wilt on a red oak is the classic oak wilt signature — infected red oaks can die in a single growing season.

Heritage Oak Deadwood & Structure

60-to-100-year oaks need a deadwood and structural pruning rotation every 2-3 years to stay sound and safe over the canopy.

Storm-Damaged Heritage Oak

A split leader or hanging limb on a mature oak is a hazard — but hazard pruning still waits for the dormant season wherever it safely can.

Getting the Timing Right

Homeowners call to schedule oak work correctly — inside the December-March or August-October windows, never the April-July prohibition.

Common Oak Questions

Oak Tree Care FAQ

Five things NE Ohio homeowners want to know before scheduling oak work.

When can oaks be pruned?
Dormant season (December-March) is the primary pruning window, and late summer (August-October) is the secondary window. Never April 1 through July 31 — oak wilt vector exposure makes fresh pruning wounds direct infection points.
My red oak is suddenly wilting from the top — is it oak wilt?
Possibly. Rapid upper-canopy wilting on a red oak is the classic oak wilt presentation. Don't wait — call {{global.phone}} for assessment. Confirmed oak wilt typically requires removal of the affected tree and root-graft trenching to protect neighboring oaks.
Are all oaks equally vulnerable to oak wilt?
No. The red oak group (red oak, pin oak, black oak, scarlet oak) is highly susceptible — infected red oaks usually die in one growing season. The white oak group (white oak, swamp white oak, bur oak) is more resistant and declines slowly over years.
How much does oak maintenance cost?
Oak maintenance pruning typically runs $400-$1,800 per tree depending on size and scope, with heritage 80+ ft oaks at the upper range. Multi-tree preservation contracts qualify for 15–20% package savings, quoted on-site.
Can I prune my own oak in summer if it's small?
No — the April 1 through July 31 prohibition applies to all oak pruning regardless of size. Sap-feeding beetles vector oak wilt to small trees just as readily as to large ones.
